comment: Shared decision table for SpfnContractBinding.requireSupported / SPFNContractBinding.requireSupported. Both platforms read this file, so a rule that drifts on one of them fails there instead of being discovered against a real server. Hand-written on purpose: these are the cases a reviewer asked for, and deriving them from the same code they test would prove nothing.
rule: supported when the candidate parses as strict SemVer and carries the same pre-release as the lower bound; a release pin then admits any core at or above it and below the upper bound, while a pre-release pin admits only its own core. cases[] drives satisfies(); parsing[] drives parse() directly, so a rule that passes for the wrong reason still fails.

a later patch on the pinned minor is additive
build metadata carries no precedence
below 1.0.0 the minor is the breaking axis; this is the case that made the rule necessary
a pre-release of a version outside the range is still outside it
a pre-release precedes its release, so it is below the lower bound

the lower bound is inclusive
at and above 1.0.0 the minor is additive
the upper bound is exclusive
